newsitem.title: USA: White House releases Clinton health information.
newsitem.headline: White House releases Clinton health information.

text.p: The White House on Friday released President Bill Clinton's medical history in an effort to respond to complaints from Republican presidential candidate Bob Dole.

Among the papers released by the White House was a report that he underwent a test for HIV, the virus that causes AIDS, in 1990 and it was negative. The test was described as part of an insurance physical.
A summary of Clinton's medical history said Clinton "has no history of hypertension, diabetes, tuberculosis, sexually transmitted disease, cancer, stroke or heart disease."

The summary, with supporting letters from doctors, went over ground already covered in Clinton's previous annual physicals, that he suffers from seasonal allergies, voice hoarseness and pre-cancerous skin eruptions due to previous history of sun exposure. He also has stomach acid occasionally and lower back pain that resulted from a 1984 ski accident.
It also said Clinton does not smoke cigarettes but "occasionally chews on cigars," drinks alcohol occasionally at social events, rarely uses caffeine and sleeps about six hours a night.
